hook: A designer on a phone app drags a curve 3 pixels right, stretches it to twice its height, then flips it. The app never redraws the curve from scratch; it changes the formula. Each drag or stretch is one small edit to the function.

prereq.why: Vertex form $y = (x - h)^2 + k$ has vertex $(h, k)$; here $h = -1$ and $k = -4$.

figure.caption: The parent $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 2f(x - 3) - 1$. Each point $(a, b)$ on $f$ moves to $(a + 3, 2b - 1)$ on $g$.

chain.effect: every output moves by $k$ (a vertical translation)
the graph moves $h$ units left when $h > 0$ (a horizontal translation)
outputs are multiplied by $a$ (a vertical dilation; reflection across the $x$-axis if $a < 0$)
inputs are scaled by $\frac{1}{b}$ (a horizontal dilation; reflection across the $y$-axis if $b < 0$)

ideas: Changes outside the function act on outputs and move the graph up, down, or stretch it vertically. Changes inside act on inputs and work in reverse.
$f(x - 3)$ moves the graph $3$ right: the old output at $0$ now appears at $x = 3$.
In $a f(x) + k$, dilate first, then shift. Domain changes come from inside changes; range changes come from outside changes.

misconception.wrong: $f(x + 4)$ moves the graph $4$ units right, because of the plus sign.
misconception.right: It moves $4$ left: $g(-4) = f(0)$, so the point that was at input $0$ is now at input $-4$.

summary: $g(x) = a f(b(x - h)) + k$ dilates and reflects $f$ by $a$ and $b$ and translates it $h$ right and $k$ up. Outside changes act on outputs and the range; inside changes act on inputs and the domain, in reverse.
